purpose: The page frame for one job and nothing else: signing in, entering a passcode, or working through a multi-step task. It is the only shell in the library defined by what it REMOVES — no primary navigation, no breadcrumb, no utility group, no search. One identity, one deliberate way out, and the task.

$finding-defined-by-subtraction: ★★ A FOCUSED SHELL IS DEFINED BY SUBTRACTION AND THAT IS THE WHOLE COMPONENT. Every other shell in this library OFFERS things — destinations, a trail, a rail, a mat. This one WITHHOLDS them, because a person four screens into a payment does not need another exit. It follows that WHAT THE ONE EXIT DOES is the central design question of the component, and it is deliberately not answered here.
$finding-progress-collision: ★★ A REAL COMPOSITION CONFLICT BETWEEN TWO ARTEFACTS, NOT A STYLE PREFERENCE. This shell publishes ONE role=progressbar with aria-valuetext 'Step 2 of 4, Recipient'. Template-wizard.reference.html (#210, wave 5, PROPOSED) publishes its OWN named step rail. Hosted together, a screen-reader user is told where they are twice, in two vocabularies, which is worse than being told once badly. ⇒ PROPOSED RULE: ONE PROGRESS STATEMENT PER SCREEN. Either the shell carries the band and the hosted template's rail is decorative (aria-hidden), or the template carries the rail and the shell is used in form=auth. Drawn as the first option because the frame outlives the step list. MEASURED: shell-auth 0 progressbars / 0 aria-current=step; shell-task 1 / 0. This has to be settled once for the library, not per file.
$finding-full-bleed-measured: THE CARD LOSES ITS BORDER AND GOES FULL-BLEED BELOW 600cqi, AND IT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED. An inset bordered card on a phone spends 32px of the only reading width there is on a rule that separates the form from nothing. MEASURED: at a 1352px container the card's computed border-top-width is 1px and padding 24px; at a 512px container and again at a 392px container it is 0px with padding '0px 16px', and the card's own width (390.0) EQUALS the shell's inner width (390.0). The rule uses TWO-CLASS selectors (`.sh-main.sh-main`, `.sh-col .sh-card`) so it cannot lose a cascade race — the same specificity discipline ds-005 turns on.
$finding-exit-label-hidden-not-removed: AT PHONE WIDTH THE EXIT CONTROL KEEPS ITS ACCESSIBLE NAME AND LOSES ITS VISIBLE LABEL. MEASURED: 150.8 x 44.0 with a 102.8 x 11.6 label box at 1352cqi, becoming 44.0 x 44.0 with a 1 x 1 label box at 392cqi, and the accessible name 'Save this payment and return to Accounts' is byte-identical in both. Hidden, never removed — Sidebar-nav's rail technique applied to a single control.
$finding-brand-is-ink: ⚠ THE BRAND IS INK HERE, NOT primary/border/default, AND IT IS A DECLARED DIVERGENCE FROM Navigations AND App-shell-top-nav. In a masthead full of navigation the red wordmark is the anchor that tells you where you are. On a sign-in screen with nothing else on the band it becomes the loudest thing on a page whose only job is a form. MEASURED: logo computes rgb(26,26,26) light / rgb(255,255,255) dark. Dave's to overturn.
$finding-skip-link-is-a-judgment: THE SKIP LINK IS KEPT AS A JUDGMENT, NOT AS BOILERPLATE. SC 2.4.1 is about blocks repeated across pages, and a 56px band with two controls is arguably marginal. It is kept because the masthead does repeat on every screen of a flow and an invisible-until-focused link costs nothing. Stated so a reviewer can disagree with the reasoning rather than with an omission.
$finding-type-divergence: No raw font-family, font-size or font-weight appears anywhere in component scope. Probe: `python3 knowledge/_validate_type_composites.py | grep -c App-shell-focused` -> 0, total exactly 1097. Ratchet contribution: 0.
$finding-breakpoints-unruled: ⚠ 900cqi AND 600cqi ARE SPECIMEN CHOICES, and this file reuses App-shell-top-nav's pair deliberately rather than adding a fourth to wave 5's spread. Probe: python3 -c "import json;print('breakpoint' in json.dumps(json.load(open('knowledge/tokens/layout.json'))).lower())" -> False.

commonPatterns: a task that must not be abandoned by accident

$relationshipsNote: Template-auth and Template-wizard are the two templates this shell exists to HOST. ⚠ Hosting Template-wizard raises $finding-progress-collision; hosting Template-auth does not. An Action-bar is the natural home for the task's own primary action and is not the site footer.

accessibility.landmarks: One <header>, <main>, <footer role="contentinfo">. ⚠ THERE IS NO <nav> LANDMARK AND THAT IS THE POINT — a focused shell has no navigation to name.
accessibility.progress: role="progressbar" with aria-labelledby, aria-valuenow/min/max and an aria-valuetext that reads as a sentence ('Step 2 of 4, Recipient') rather than a bare number. One per screen — see $finding-progress-collision.
accessibility.bypassBlock: A skip link is the first focusable element, visible only on focus, targeting <main>. Kept as a judgment; see $finding-skip-link-is-a-judgment.
accessibility.exitControl: The one way out is a <button> with an aria-label that says what leaving DOES, not merely that it leaves. Its visible label is hidden at phone width; its accessible name never changes.
accessibility.targetSize: Every interactive element measures >= 44px. Driven sweep returns an empty list at every width and both themes.
accessibility.colourIsNeverAlone: Nothing in this shell carries meaning by hue. There is no red at all (redPaintCount = 0), and progress is a monochrome fill against a monochrome track — the SHAPE of the fill is the signal.
accessibility.reducedMotion: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce collapses every transition to 0.01ms, and Progress-bar's own named suppression of the fill transition is copied rather than assumed covered.

responsive.mechanism: CONTAINER queries on the shell (container-type:inline-size, container-name:shell), never viewport queries. s210-D3. Every rule targets a DESCENDANT of .sh — an element is a query container for what is inside it, never for itself.
responsive.full: >= 900cqi — the column sits at its max-width (420 for auth, 720 for task) with 48px of air above it; the card is bordered; the exit control shows its label.
responsive.compact: 600–899cqi — the air shrinks to 32px and the side padding to 24px. Nothing else moves. MEASURED at 852: card border still 1px, main padding '32px 24px'.
responsive.phone: < 600cqi — the card loses its border and goes full-bleed, and the exit control drops its visible label while keeping its accessible name. MEASURED at 512 and at a 392px container inside a 1400px viewport.
responsive.$proof: The third specimen is a 392px CONTAINER at the same viewport as the two wide ones and it is fully collapsed while they are not.

dimensions.$note: mastheadHeight 56 is Headers' in-app band, not Navigations' 64 — a frame with no navigation in it does not need the taller row. trackHeight 4 is Progress-bar's default. 420 and 720 are this file's and are named as specimen choices, not ruled measures.

antiPatterns: Never put the primary navigation back in. The moment a focused shell offers five destinations it has become App-shell-top-nav and the user has five new ways to abandon the task.
Never make the exit a bare glyph on a multi-step task. A ✕ with no name discards work silently, and the user cannot tell whether it saves.
Never carry two progress statements on one screen. Pick the shell's band or the template's step rail — see $finding-progress-collision.
Never put a doormat footer here. A mega-footer at the end of a sign-in form is a list of ways to leave.
Never keep a bordered card at phone width. It costs reading width and separates the form from nothing.
Never use form=task for a single-screen job. A progress bar reading 'step 1 of 1' is an insult to the reader.

provenance.$note: Itinerary row 101, 'App shell — focused / full-page', Shells (Layer 2), P3, notes cell 'Auth / wizard frame.' Derived verdict NO-ARTEFACT-CLASS. Built #210 wave 6 lane A.

$decisionsForDave: 1 · ⛔ WHAT DOES THE ONE EXIT DO? This is the central question of the component and it is deliberately unanswered. Does 'Save and exit' save a draft? Does 'Exit' on a half-finished payment discard it silently? Does it need a Popconfirm or a Modal? The library has both. Until this is ruled, the exit control is a labelled button with a descriptive accessible name and no confirmed behaviour.

2 · ⛔ ONE PROGRESS STATEMENT PER SCREEN — confirm or overturn, once, for the whole library. Drawn as: the shell owns the numeric band, a hosted wizard's step rail is decorative. The alternative is the opposite assignment. Either is defensible; having both is not.

3 · THE BRAND IN INK RATHER THAN RED. Navigations and App-shell-top-nav paint the wordmark primary/border/default. This shell paints it text/default because there is nothing else on the band for it to compete with. Confirm or overturn.
4 · THE BREAKPOINT SCALE — carried, wave-wide, unruled.

5 · THE BRAND MARK. 12 official SVGs sit in knowledge/assets/logos/ and nothing binds them; zero of the pre-existing snippets reference them; row 86's derived verdict is ASSET-ONLY. An auth screen is the single most likely place a real masterbrand lock-up belongs. Carried from wave 5, unresolved.
6 · THE TWO COLUMN WIDTHS — 420 for auth and 720 for task. Specimen choices. Is there a measure scale, or should these be tokens?
7 · DOES A SHELL BELONG IN knowledge/snippets/ AT ALL? Carried from wave 5 unchanged.
8 · SHOULD THE FOCUSED SHELL OFFER A 'HELP' AFFORDANCE? Drawn without one, deliberately — but a person stuck on a passcode screen with no navigation and no help has nowhere to go but away.
